Controller and Registry In Managed Controller mode, TrustedRegistry (registry.yaml) and ControllerConfig (controller.yaml) separate operator-approved execution authority from task requests (see Configuration relationships ). The operator stores registry.yaml (metadata.name) outside any writable repository, pins exact handler and runtime SHA-256 digests, and locks registry.yaml inside controller.yaml by name and SHA-256 (--registry-sha256).

update release manifest" Handlers and profiles Handler implementations Each TrustedRegistry.spec.handlers[] entry pins id, version: 1, digest (installed file SHA-256 from installedHandlerDigests()), kind, implementation, parameters, and exact capabilities:
Implementation kind Required capabilities Required parameters keys pi.agent.v1 agent ['pi'] prompt (string), purpose ('task' or 'review') pi.compact.v1 agent ['pi', 'compaction'] {} (empty mapping; compacts session context) scope.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId (identifier or null for implicit guard) json-artifact.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId, path, required (key list), equals (scalar map) no-change.v1 check ['inert_bytes', 'read_only'] checkId (identifier or null for implicit comparison) gate.v1 check ['external_service', 'read_only'] checkId, endpointRef (gateEndpoints[].id), gateId Role and runtime profiles Top-level TrustedRegistry requires metadata.name (1..64 chars) and spec (version: 1, resourceVersion, handlers, roleProfiles, resources, runtimeProfiles, credentialBindings, environmentBindings; gateEndpoints and publicationEndpoints are optional keys):
Field path Required Values and bounds Meaning roleProfiles[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique role profile ID referenced by ControllerConfig roleProfiles[].selection Yes { provider, model, thinking, api, customProvider? } (off..max; anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses) Token-based Pi model or custom compatible endpoint; see Model configuration roleProfiles[].tools Yes Subset of read, write, edit, bash, codemode, mcp__workspace__read_file Host-approved tool ceiling for bound task roles roleProfiles[].runtimeRef Yes runtimeProfiles[].id Binds the role to a verified runtime identity roleProfiles[].providerCredentialRef Yes (null allowed) credentialBindings[].id or null Selects the provider credential injected into the broker runtimeProfiles[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique runtime profile ID runtimeProfiles[].dockerExecutable Yes Absolute path (for example /usr/local/bin/docker) Verified container runtime binary path runtimeProfiles[].dockerSocket Yes Absolute path (for example /var/run/docker.sock) Container runtime UNIX socket path runtimeProfiles[].identity Yes sdkIntegrity, graphDigest (package-lock.json SHA-256), imageDigest (sha256:...), configDigest, profile: 'linux/arm64' Cryptographic runtime lock from describePiAdapterFiles() Context and MCP bounds Context window fields roleProfiles[].context prevents oversized prompts from truncating safety instructions or blowing provider windows:
Field path Required Values and bounds Meaning context.mode No 'proven_bound' (default) or 'estimated_guard' Strict pre-send byte proof vs. estimated window guard context.estimator Yes 'lw-pi-final-json-bytes-v1' Deterministic JSON request byte estimator context.proofId / version / evidence Yes proofId: null, version: 1, evidence: 'estimated' Estimator protocol metadata required by Pi adapter context.workingWindowCeiling Yes Integer 1 .. 98304 bytes Maximum retained conversation window bytes before compaction context.maxRequestBytes Yes Integer 1 .. 65536 bytes Maximum single outbound provider HTTP payload size context.serviceMargin Yes Integer >= 32768 bytes Safety buffer reserved for provider system framing context.toolReserve Yes Integer >= 16384 bytes Window space reserved for tool call results context.maxOutputTokens Yes Integer 1 .. 1024 tokens Per-call output token ceiling enforced by the adapter MCP configuration roleProfiles[].mcp (serverId: 'workspace') is required on every roleProfiles[] entry and supports two modes (names: ['mcp__workspace__read_file'] and effects: ['read_only'] when mcp__workspace__read_file is in tools, or [] when unused; idleTimeoutSeconds: 1..2, absoluteTimeoutSeconds: idle..10):
MCP mode Required keys Security constraint Local script mode serverId, scriptDigest, names, effects, idleTimeoutSeconds, absoluteTimeoutSeconds Verifies local MCP helper against localMcpScriptDigest Remote HTTP mode Replaces scriptDigest with transport: 'sessionless-http-json-v1', destinationRef, endpoint, approvedAddresses, credentialRef Requires https://<hostname>/mcp (or http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp) and pinned IP addresses (1..4 IPs) to block DNS rebinding Credentials and endpoints Credential and env bindings Secrets resolve only in memory into a CredentialVault ($$ escapes a literal $), and vault.assertClean aborts if raw secret bytes ever appear in serialized config or state:
Field path Required Values and bounds Meaning credentialBindings[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique credential ID referenced by profiles or endpoints credentialBindings[].consumer Yes 'provider' | 'mcp' | 'gate' | 'publisher' Restricts which subsystem may receive the resolved secret credentialBindings[].destinationRef Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Target service identifier bound to the credential credentialBindings[].environmentNames Yes Env var list ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) Host environment variables permitted inside template credentialBindings[].template Yes Template string (for example ${LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN}) Secret assembly pattern matched identically in ControllerConfig.spec.credentials environmentBindings[].name Yes Env var name ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) Approved host environment variable name environmentBindings[].classification Yes 'credential' or 'nonsecret' Marks whether resolved values are scrubbed as secrets environmentBindings[].paths Yes JSON pointer list (/spec/credentials/<n>/template or /spec/task/...) Exact ControllerConfig paths allowed to reference name Environment interpolation Loopwright expands ${NAME} ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) inside ControllerConfig in a single pass (<= 16 KiB per string) before validating the embedded TaskContract:
Escape and non-execution: Write $$ for a literal $ ($${NAME} stays ${NAME}). Shell command substitution $(...), !command resolvers, and ${NAME:-default} fallbacks never execute (CONFIG_ENV_SYNTAX). JSON Pointer allowlist: Every ${NAME} must match TrustedRegistry.spec.environmentBindings[] at that exact JSON Pointer (CONFIG_ENV_DENIED if unlisted, CONFIG_ENV_MISSING if unset): credential is restricted to /spec/credentials/<n>/template, whereas nonsecret injects non-credential values such as /spec/task/spec/target/sourceRevision. Untrusted manifests: In-repo .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (kind: Taskpack) rejects ${...} (TASKPACK_UNTRUSTED_INTERPOLATION) and binds host variables by name via spec.models[].apiKeyEnv. Gate and publication endpoints spec.gateEndpoints and spec.publicationEndpoints are optional top-level keys in TrustedRegistry (0..16 items). When an item is declared, all keys below are required (https:// or loopback http://127.0.0.1:<port> / http://[::1]:<port> with zero URL credentials, query strings, or # fragments):
Field path Required Bounds Meaning gateEndpoints / publicationEndpoints No 0 .. 16 items (optional keys) Omit when unused; required when gate.v1 or pull_request publication is bound *.id / *.url Conditional Identifier (1..64) / HTTPS URL Required per endpoint item; unique ID and target service URL gateEndpoints[].signingCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id (consumer: gate) Required per gate item; HMAC key verifying gate.v1 receipts gateEndpoints[].authCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id or null Required per gate item (null when no bearer header is used) gateEndpoints[].timeoutMs / maxPollMs Conditional 1000 .. 60000 ms / 1000 .. 600000 ms Required per gate item; per-request and total polling timeouts gateEndpoints[].pollInitialMs / pollMaxMs Conditional 100 .. 30000 ms / pollInitialMs .. maxPollMs Required per gate item; exponential backoff polling interval bounds gateEndpoints[].jitter Conditional 0 .. 1000 ms Required per gate item; random jitter added between gate polls publicationEndpoints[].signingCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id (consumer: publisher) Required per publication item; HMAC key verifying PR receipts publicationEndpoints[].authCredentialRef Conditional credentialBindings[].id or null Required per publication item (null when unused) publicationEndpoints[].timeoutMs Conditional 1000 .. 60000 ms Required per publication item; HTTP timeout for PR requests Controller controls Field path Required Bounds and values Meaning spec.task Yes Complete TaskContract object Embedded task contract bound into the run spec.registry.name / digest Yes Registry metadata.name + 64-char SHA-256 Must match registry.yaml bytes and --registry-sha256 CLI flag spec.profiles.roles Yes { roleId, profileRef } (0..16 items) Connects each TaskContract role to a TrustedRegistry RoleProfile spec.profiles.steps Yes { stepId, handlerRef } (0..16 items) Connects each TaskContract step to a TrustedRegistry Handler spec.credentials Yes { ref, template } list (pass [] if none) Declares credential templates interpolated from approved env vars controls.drainReserveMs Yes 120000 .. 300000 ms (< budgets.wallTimeMs) Time reserved before wallTimeMs to drain processes and persist state controls.maxAttempts Yes 1 .. 16 Total execution and repair attempts allowed across the cycle controls.repeatFailureLimit Yes 2 Stops repair loops when the exact same failure signature occurs twice controls.submission Yes mode: 'artifact_or_assistant', path: null or relative path Accepts candidate output from a named workspace file or final assistant turn spec.publication No Defaults to { mode: 'disabled' }; or { mode: 'pull_request', endpointRef, targetBranch, headBranchPrefix, titleTemplate } Optional block; when mode: 'pull_request', all four PR keys are required Recovery Gates and reconciliation Run loopwright check or loopwright run --dry-run before execution. When an external gate or pull request call terminates in an uncertain state (unknown), never replay the side effect blindly; verify the remote state and settle the run with loopwright reconcile and an authenticated receipt.

Decision Routing System-One decision routing uses fast, calibrated models to classify bounded triage questions (such as retry classification, scope pre-screening, or review routing). Routing is strictly advisory: deterministic controller gates and TrustedRegistry rules retain full authority over execution, verification, and publication.
Contents DecisionPolicy Confidence zones Policy reference Fallback and authority DecisionPolicy Standalone host policy (decisions.yaml): Load a DecisionPolicy document via loadDecisionPolicyFile('decisions.yaml') in custom controller or App integrations. Declarative Taskpack (spec.decisions): Embed the same fields under spec.decisions in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (Taskpack validates the block and exposes it to host callers; runGitHubActionEntrypoint does not instantiate a live provider automatically). yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: DecisionPolicy spec: enabled: true # Optional in standalone decisions.yaml (defaults to false) disclosurePolicy: public-metadata-only # Optional (defaults to disabled) provider: typesafe-jev # Optional (defaults to typesafe-jev) minConfidence: 0.8 # Optional (defaults to 0.8) confirmThreshold: 0.6 # Optional (defaults to 0.6) hardDeadlineMs: 5000 # Optional (defaults to 5000) maxAttempts: 1 # Optional (defaults to 1) allowImages: false # Optional (defaults to false) Taskpack nesting: Inside .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (kind: Taskpack), place the spec.* fields under spec.decisions rather than repeating a nested DecisionPolicy header. Threshold order: Validation rejects policies where confirmThreshold > minConfidence (DECISION_POLICY_INVALID). Confidence zones Every calibrated response is routed into one of three deterministic zones based on minConfidence and confirmThreshold:
Zone Confidence range Router action act confidence >= minConfidence Accepts the advisory choice within bounded non-authority scope confirm confirmThreshold <= confidence < minConfidence Requests secondary confirmation or conservative check escalate confidence < confirmThreshold (or timeout/error) Rejects model advice and executes deterministic fallback Policy reference Policy fields In a standalone DecisionPolicy document (decisions.yaml), apiVersion, kind, and spec are required while all spec.* keys default cleanly; when nested under Taskpack spec.decisions, decisions.enabled is required and the remaining 7 shared fields are optional:
Field path Required Default Bounds and meaning apiVersion / kind Conditional — Required in standalone envelope (loopwright.dev/v1alpha1, DecisionPolicy); omit in taskpack.yaml spec.enabled Conditional false Required inside Taskpack spec.decisions; optional in standalone decisions.yaml spec.disclosurePolicy No 'disabled' Outbound payload redaction tier (disabled, public-metadata-only, repo-approved-redacted-evidence) spec.provider No 'typesafe-jev' Target provider adapter and wire dialect spec.minConfidence No 0.8 Float in 0.5 .. 1.0; minimum calibrated score required for act spec.confirmThreshold No 0.6 Float in 0.0 .. 1.0 (<= minConfidence); floor for confirm before escalate spec.hardDeadlineMs No 5000 Integer 100 .. 30000 ms shared across all attempts spec.maxAttempts No 1 1 (single call) or 2 (one retry if time remains in hardDeadlineMs) spec.allowImages No false Permits image inputs and box bounding-box questions when true spec.endpoint / spec.model No Provider default Standalone DecisionPolicy only: custom http(s):// URL and model ID override spec.fallbackRole No null Standalone DecisionPolicy only: fallback role ID or null spec.onFallbackUnavailable No 'blocked' Standalone DecisionPolicy only: 'blocked' or 'deterministic_default' spec.startluxOptions No null Standalone DecisionPolicy only: thinkMode, thinkBudget, gate, allowNone tuning Providers Provider Wire dialect Default model Secret variable typesafe-jev systemone jev-latest TYPESAFE_API_KEY openai-decisions openai-decisions gpt-6-luna OPENAI_API_KEY startlux-decision systemone startlux-decision-27b-autothink STARTLUX_API_KEY microsoft-decision systemone microsoft-decision-1 MICROSOFT_DECISION_API_KEY perplexity-decider systemone pplx-decider-v1.2 PERPLEXITY_API_KEY cloudflare-clef systemone @cf/cloudflare/clef CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN liquid-d1 systemone liquid/d1-ultra LIQUID_API_KEY Disclosure policies Policy Outbound payload ceiling Security rule disabled 0 bytes (no network call) Blocks all outbound provider requests public-metadata-only Redacted metadata (<= 512 chars) Strips raw file contents, diffs, and secrets repo-approved-redacted-evidence Secret-scrubbed evidence (<= 64 KiB) Requires explicit operator approval for repository snippets Question primitives Programmatic @loopwright/decisions callers compose structured requests from four primitives:
Primitive Output shape Constraint choice Single option key (<= 255 options) Supported across all seven providers score Weighted score across 2..10 criteria Supported across all seven providers noul Calibrated binary probability (0.0..1.0) Supported across all seven providers box Normalized bounding box coordinates Requires allowImages: true and vision-capable provider Fallback and authority Six safety-critical intents (such as bypassing verification receipts, expanding writable scope, or overriding lease fences) are permanently non-delegable and never sent to a decision model. When a provider is disabled, unreachable, or returns low confidence, Loopwright falls back to deterministic rules and retains any uncertain provider consumption in run observations.
See also — Taskpack (embed spec.decisions in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml) · Controller and Registry (deterministic controller authority)

Sandbox Backends Sandbox policy negotiates OS or container isolation before any agent step runs. When available host backends cannot satisfy your requested capabilities or network policy, negotiation fails closed (SANDBOX_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE or SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT).
Contents Sandbox policy Policy fields Backend choices Network and capabilities Host qualification Sandbox policy Declarative Taskpack mode: Declare spec.sandbox inside .loopwright/taskpack.yaml. The GitHub Action or App negotiates a matching host backend automatically. Managed Controller mode: Pin container/runtime identities in TrustedRegistry.spec.runtimeProfiles[] (see Controller and Registry ) and pass SandboxPolicyInput when invoking native host sandbox wrappers. yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: docs-sync spec: # Other Taskpack sections omitted; see Taskpack. sandbox: # Optional host isolation policy preferredBackends: # Optional priority order - macos-seatbelt - linux-bwrap - linux-landlock - docker networkMode: none # Optional (defaults to none) requiredCapabilities: # Optional - filesystemReadContainment - filesystemWriteContainment - protectedPathReadOnlyMask - networkIsolation - processTreeCleanup deniedReadPaths: # Optional extra host paths masked unreadable - ~/.ssh - ~/.aws - ~/.config/gh Priority order: Loopwright probes preferredBackends in order and picks the first backend supporting every listed requiredCapabilities item. Declared policy: Omitting networkMode in an explicit sandbox policy defaults to none. Additive path masks: deniedReadPaths supplements built-in .github, .loopwright/policies, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md protections. When GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and spec.sandbox is omitted, resolveEffectiveTaskpackSandboxPolicy selects direct-dedicated. It sets allow-outbound, requires processTreeCleanup, and enables allowDedicatedDirectOverride. GitHub-hosted runner VMs isolate jobs, but direct execution does not add filesystem or network masks. The same default applies to self-hosted Actions runners; confirm their isolation before use.
The turnkey host session supports macos-seatbelt, linux-bwrap, linux-landlock, and direct-dedicated, and blocks docker.
Without GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, an omitted policy selects fail-closed macos-seatbelt, linux-bwrap, or linux-landlock negotiation.
Policy fields spec.sandbox itself is optional inside Taskpack, and every subfield inside spec.sandbox is also optional:
Field path Required Default and bounds Meaning spec.sandbox No Unset Optional sandbox declaration block in Taskpack sandbox.preferredBackends No Host default order (1..5 unique) Ordered candidate backends probed on the execution host sandbox.networkMode No 'none' ('none', 'loopback-only', 'allow-outbound') Socket policy enforced at the OS or container boundary sandbox.requiredCapabilities No Unset (0..6 unique) Isolation guarantees that the chosen backend must provide sandbox.deniedReadPaths No Unset (0..64 entries) Host or ~/-relative paths blocked from read access Backend choices Configure spec.sandbox.preferredBackends[] in priority order:
Backend Isolation mechanism Host prerequisite macos-seatbelt macOS Seatbelt profile (sandbox-exec) Qualified macOS host with /usr/bin/sandbox-exec linux-bwrap Linux namespaces and seccomp (bwrap) Qualified Linux host with /usr/bin/bwrap linux-landlock Linux Landlock LSM rules Linux kernel with Landlock ABI support docker Rootless or daemon container Qualified Docker binary and verified daemon socket direct-dedicated Disposable dedicated runner Actions default for omitted policy; otherwise explicit host opt-in; no filesystem/network masks Network and capabilities Network modes Mode Traffic policy Constraint none Blocks all outbound and loopback sockets Default for an explicit policy without networkMode loopback-only Permits 127.0.0.1 and ::1 traffic only Used for local loopback MCP or runner bridges allow-outbound Permits outbound network connections Actions omitted-policy default or explicit policy opt-in Sandbox capabilities Capability Protection boundary Supporting backends filesystemReadContainment Restricts reads outside workspace and deniedReadPaths Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker filesystemWriteContainment Restricts writes strictly to candidate writable paths Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker protectedPathReadOnlyMask Mounts or masks protected paths read-only Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker networkIsolation Enforces networkMode at kernel or container level Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, Docker processTreeCleanup Terminates all descendant processes on step exit All five backends syscallFiltering Applies seccomp or container syscall filter profile Bubblewrap and Docker Host qualification Live observations Local fixture checks do not qualify a production host. Before relying on a backend in CI or production, verify the host OS/architecture (darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, linux/x64), installed sandbox binaries, and kernel user-namespace or Landlock support.
Limits and costs Resource limits, timeouts, and token consumption depend on the approved RuntimeProfile and TaskContract.spec.budgets envelope.
See also — Taskpack (embed spec.sandbox in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml) · Controller and Registry (pin runtimeProfiles in registry.yaml)

Task Contract TaskContract defines what bounded work is requested, where files may change, how much time and model budget a run may spend, and which independent checks must pass. In Declarative Taskpack mode, Loopwright compiles TaskContract automatically; in Managed Controller mode, you embed TaskContract inside ControllerConfig (controller.yaml) while keeping credentials and handler digests in TrustedRegistry (see Configuration relationships ).
Contents TaskContract Envelope and target Scope and context Roles and steps Budgets and enforcement Acceptance and evidence TaskContract yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TaskContract spec: goal: Update packages/app/manifest.json release metadata and pass verification. taskpack: app-manifest target: repository: acme/example-app baseRevision: 67a4938 sourceRevision: v1.4.0 matrix: null # Optional matrix cell list (use null for controller runs) scope: writable: - "packages/app/**" protected: - "packages/app/policy/**" roles: - id: builder adapter: pi provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high tools: - read - write - edit trustedContext: revision: rev-2026-11 discovery: disabled resources: # Optional pinned context files (use [] when unused) - id: release-guide kind: instruction path: context/release-guide.md digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> budgets: wallTimeMs: 300000 totalTokens: 64000 perCallOutputTokens: 1024 maxModelCalls: 8 maxConcurrency: 1 maxFormatRepairs: 1 maxImplementationRepairs: 2 maxTransportRetries: 1 enforcement: wallTime: hard_admission tokens: soft_accounting modelCalls: hard_admission concurrency: hard_admission formatRepairs: hard_admission implementationRepairs: hard_admission transportRetries: hard_admission steps: - id: author-change kind: agent uses: pi-author roleId: builder dependsOn: [] - id: verify-manifest kind: check uses: check-manifest-json roleId: null # Optional on schema; null for check steps dependsOn: - author-change acceptance: required: - manifest-json checks: - id: manifest-json allowedEvidenceLevels: - local_execution Zero embedded authority: TaskContract cannot approve handler code, environment variables, network endpoints, or credentials. Deterministic canonicalization: Loopwright hashes TaskContract via RFC 8785 JCS (taskByteDigest) so any field edit produces a distinct run identity. Envelope and target Strict contractSchema validation requires apiVersion, kind, and spec and requires every declared spec key below to appear explicitly (null or [] where empty; unknown or omitted keys fail with FIELD_REQUIRED or FIELD_UNKNOWN):
Field path Required Type and bounds Meaning apiVersion Yes 'loopwright.dev/v1alpha1' Unified Loopwright document version kind Yes 'TaskContract' Selects strict contractSchema validation (<= 1 MiB input) spec.goal Yes String (1..4096 chars) Plain-language objective evaluated by roles and recorded in receipts spec.taskpack Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Logical taskpack or workflow identifier (Taskpack.metadata.name) spec.target.repository Yes Repo slug (1..256 chars) Target owner/repo path ([A-Za-z0-9._/-]+) spec.target.baseRevision Yes Revision (1..128 chars) Base commit SHA, tag, or branch checked out before agent execution spec.target.sourceRevision Yes Revision (1..128 chars) Upstream release, tag, or commit revision that triggered the work spec.target.matrix Yes (null allowed) null or cell list (1..64) Target matrix ({ id, platform, variant }); set null for controller runs Scope and context Field path Required Type and bounds Meaning spec.scope.writable Yes Glob list (1..128 patterns) Relative path globs where candidate edits are permitted spec.scope.protected Yes Glob list (0..128 patterns) Read-only globs overriding writable (pass [] if none) trustedContext.revision Yes Revision (1..128 chars) Version label for pinned supplementary context files trustedContext.discovery Yes 'disabled' Disables unpinned workspace prompt discovery so all context is hash-bound trustedContext.resources Yes Object list (0..128 items) Read-only context files (<= 1 MiB total; pass [] when unused) resources[].id Conditional Identifier (1..64 chars) Required per item; matches TrustedRegistry.spec.resources[].id resources[].kind Conditional 'instruction' | 'skill' | 'document' Required per item; declares how runtime mounts the context file resources[].path Conditional Relative path (1..1024 chars) Required per item; path resolved under TrustedRegistry directory resources[].digest Conditional { algorithm: 'sha256', hex } Required per item; 64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex digest Turnkey taskpacks protect .github, .claude, .codex, .agents, .loopwright/policies, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md by default.

Validation fails with BUDGET_INCONSISTENT if any per-call or retry cap exceeds its parent ceiling:
Field path Required Type and constraint Meaning budgets.wallTimeMs Yes Integer (>= 1 ms) Total wall-clock timeout; must exceed ControllerConfig.spec.controls.drainReserveMs budgets.totalTokens Yes Integer (>= 1) Cumulative prompt + completion token ceiling across the entire run budgets.perCallOutputTokens Yes Integer (1 .. totalTokens) Maximum completion tokens per model call (<= 1024 in Pi profiles) budgets.maxModelCalls Yes Integer (>= 1) Maximum total model API invocations across authoring, compaction, and repairs budgets.maxConcurrency Yes Integer (1 .. maxModelCalls) Maximum steps dispatched concurrently by the scheduler budgets.maxFormatRepairs Yes Integer (0 .. maxModelCalls) Allowed repair turns when agent output fails structured submission parsing budgets.maxImplementationRepairs Yes Integer (0 .. maxModelCalls) Allowed repair turns after an independent check or gate reports failure budgets.maxTransportRetries Yes Integer (0 .. maxModelCalls) Allowed retries on transient network/provider transport failures budgets.enforcement.* Yes All 7 dimension keys Enforcement mode for wallTime, tokens, modelCalls, concurrency, formatRepairs, implementationRepairs, transportRetries Enforcement modes Configure spec.budgets.enforcement.<dimension> for each of the seven dimensions (wallTime, tokens, modelCalls, concurrency, formatRepairs, implementationRepairs, transportRetries):
Mode Admission behavior Controller usage hard_admission Pre-reserves quota in SQLite before dispatch; refuses dispatch if remaining allowance is insufficient Required for wallTime, modelCalls, concurrency, formatRepairs, implementationRepairs, and transportRetries soft_accounting Records actual post-call usage and halts subsequent calls once ceiling is reached Used for tokens because exact output token counts are only known after model generation Acceptance and evidence Artifact manifests An ArtifactManifest uses one of two mutually exclusive spec shapes. Classic { entries } supports up to 256 entries. Admission selects it only if the baseline has at most 128 files and 4 MiB total bytes. Its canonical manifest JSON must fit 32 KiB and its inventory JSON must fit 256 KiB.
Otherwise, admission selects tree_overlay with { baseTree, entries, deleted }. The baseline supports up to 65,536 regular files. The overlay supports up to 128 added or modified entries, 128 deleted paths, and 4 MiB of aggregate entry bytes.

title: Task Contract

content:
Taskpack Taskpack powers Loopwright’s automated mode. Declare repository intent in a bounded YAML document (<= 64 KiB), such as .loopwright/taskpack.yaml or .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml. The host compiles runtime contracts, handler SHA-256 digests, and credential bindings.
For multi-step DAGs or operator-owned TrustedRegistry files stored outside the repository, use Managed Controller mode (Task Contract and Controller and Registry ).
Contents Compilation model Taskpack Metadata and scope Model configuration MCP and limits Upstreams and proposal Verification checks Publication and memory Triggers and policies Output formats Compilation model When a GitHub Action or App processes a taskpack, compileDeclarativeTaskpack generates three runtime artifacts:
Generated artifact Manifest inputs Compiler defaults TaskContract metadata.name, spec.goal, spec.scope, spec.verification, spec.limits Adds protected paths and default budgets (wallTimeMs: 3600000, maxModelCalls: 256) TrustedRegistry spec.proposal, spec.verification, spec.publication, spec.mcp Computes SHA-256 digests for installed handlers (pi.agent.v1, json-artifact.v1, scope.v1, no-change.v1, gate.v1) and package-lock.json ControllerConfig Binds compiled TaskContract and TrustedRegistry SHA-256 Sets drainReserveMs: 120000, maxAttempts: 4, repeatFailureLimit: 2, and ${ENV} credential templates (0600) Turnkey compilation grants author roles ['read', 'write', 'edit', 'bash', 'delete'] plus discovered mcp__<id>__<tool> tools.

manifests - docs/versions.md protected: # Optional blacklist - manifests/frozen-policy.yaml instructions: # Optional protected UTF-8 instruction files - .loopwright/instructions.md upstreams: - id: engine-release kind: github-release source: octocat/engine watchedPaths: - json - github-step-summary sandbox: # Optional host isolation policy preferredBackends: # Optional - macos-seatbelt - linux-bwrap - linux-landlock - docker networkMode: none # Optional (defaults to none) requiredCapabilities: # Optional - filesystemReadContainment - filesystemWriteContainment - protectedPathReadOnlyMask - networkIsolation - processTreeCleanup deniedReadPaths: # Optional - ~/.ssh decisions: # Optional System-One triage policy enabled: true provider: typesafe-jev # Optional (defaults to typesafe-jev) disclosurePolicy: public-metadata-only # Optional (defaults to disabled) minConfidence: 0.8 # Optional (defaults to 0.8) confirmThreshold: 0.6 # Optional (defaults to 0.6) hardDeadlineMs: 5000 # Optional (defaults to 5000) maxAttempts: 1 # Optional (defaults to 1) allowImages: false # Optional (defaults to false) Strict YAML 1.2: The parser rejects symlinks (O_NOFOLLOW), .. traversal, duplicate keys, YAML anchors/aliases, and ${NAME} interpolation (TASKPACK_UNTRUSTED_INTERPOLATION; see Environment interpolation ). Control root: Set Action taskpack-path to select a manifest. Its parent becomes the control root. Root fallback: Root-level manifests and raw bytes use .loopwright as the control root. Built-in masks: PROTECTED_AUTOMATION_PATHS protects .github, .claude, .codex, .agents, .loopwright/policies, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md. Control root mask: The active control root also remains protected. Protected assets: The exact manifest path, instruction files, and command scripts also remain protected. Metadata and scope Field path Required Type and bounds Meaning apiVersion Yes 'loopwright.dev/v1alpha1' Unified Loopwright schema version kind Yes 'Taskpack' Selects declarative taskpack validation (<= 64 KiB) metadata.name Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique lowercase slug ([a-z][a-z0-9._-]*); scopes tenant queue and TaskContract.spec.taskpack spec.goal.candidate Yes String (1..1024 chars) Prompt objective compiled when candidate edits are expected spec.goal.noChange Yes String (1..1024 chars) Prompt objective compiled when verifying no_change eligibility spec.scope No Object Writable whitelist and protected blacklist; both fields may be omitted spec.scope.writable No String list (1..128 paths) Relative paths open for writes; omission allows the repository subject to protected paths spec.scope.protected No String list (0..128 paths) Relative paths excluded from writes in addition to built-in masks spec.instructions No Relative path or list (1..16 paths) UTF-8 files compiled as SHA-256-pinned instruction trusted resources; aggregate size <= 262144 bytes Scope paths name a file or directory and include descendants. Raw globs, traversal, and spaces are not accepted. Protected paths always win, so a writable ancestor may contain protected descendants. A writable path covered by a protected path is rejected. An explicit empty writable list is invalid. The proposal path must remain writable after exclusions.
Instruction files must be regular files without symlinks in the path. The manifest path also rejects symlinked ancestors.
Model configuration Loopwright inherits provider, model, thinking, wire api, and custom models.json semantics from the Pi model catalog and Pi’s providers , models , and models-configuration guides. spec.models declares an ordered 1..8 candidate list for the coding and authoring LLM (separate from spec.decisions triage).
Loopwright admits token-authenticated HTTP providers only and handles rate spikes and quota limits across two layers:
Supported built-in token providers: zai (ZAI_API_KEY) and zai-coding-cn (ZAI_CODING_CN_API_KEY) ship glm-5.3 (thinking: off, low, high, max), alongside anthropic, openai, openrouter, deepseek, qwen-token-plan, qwen-token-plan-cn, fireworks, together, baseten, nvidia, groq, cerebras, mistral, xai, huggingface, minimax, minimax-cn, moonshotai, kimi-coding, opencode, vercel-ai-gateway, xiaomi, and ant-ling. Supported custom gateways: Declare baseUrl and api (openai-completions, openai-responses, or anthropic-messages) in any spec.models[] item (with Action allow-custom-base-url: 'true') or supply a host Pi models.json file (models-json). Quota probe and fallback: A single candidate runs with zero probe overhead; >= 2 candidates (or comma-separated tokens in apiKeyEnv) run a max_tokens=1 preflight probe (<= 15s each, <= 30s total) to skip 402, 400 quota codes (1113), 401/403, 429, or 5xx, while maxTransportRetries absorbs transient 429 bursts in-session and rotates to the next candidate on mid-run quota exhaustion. Refused OAuth and shell providers: Interactive OAuth/CLI providers (github-copilot, gemini, google, gemini-cli, google-gemini-cli, google-antigravity, claude-code, openai-codex), oauth blocks, literal apiKey secrets, and !command shell resolvers fail closed with PROVIDER_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED. yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: catalog-sync spec: # Other Taskpack sections omitted; see Taskpack above. models: # Optional ordered model pool - provider: custom-glm-gateway id: glm-5.3 thinking: high # Optional api: openai-completions # Optional for built-in providers; needed with baseUrl baseUrl: https://llm-gateway.example.com/v1 # Optional custom endpoint URL apiKeyEnv: ZAI_API_KEY # Optional authHeader: true # Optional Bearer header toggle contextWindow: 204800 # Optional maxTokens: 32768 # Optional reasoning: true # Optional samplingParams: # Optional temperature: 0.6 top_p: 0.95 compat: # Optional OpenAI-compatible wire dialect tuning thinkingFormat: zai maxTokensField: max_tokens zaiToolStream: true - provider: zai-coding-cn # Optional fallback candidate id: glm-5.3 thinking: high # Optional apiKeyEnv: ZAI_CODING_CN_API_KEY # Optional Model fields Field path Required Type and bounds Meaning spec.models No Object list (1..8 items; zai/glm-5.3/high default) Ordered coding model candidates; Action provider/model inputs override the list models[].provider Conditional Slug (1..64 chars) Required per item; token-based Pi provider or custom provider ID models[].id Conditional Model ID (1..128 chars) Required per item; model identifier (for example glm-5.3) models[].thinking No 'off' | 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max' Reasoning effort validated against Pi reasoning and thinkingLevelMap models[].api Conditional 'anthropic-messages' | 'openai-completions' | 'openai-responses' Required when models[].baseUrl is set; inferred for built-in Pi providers models[].apiKeyEnv No Env var name ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) Host env var holding API token or comma-separated tokens (defaults to Pi env or LOOPWRIGHT_PROVIDER_TOKEN) models[].baseUrl No https:// URL (or loopback http://127.0.0.1:<port>) Custom compatible API base URL; requires host allowManifestCustomBaseUrl models[].authHeader No Boolean Forces Authorization: Bearer <token> on custom anthropic-messages endpoints models[].headers No String map (<= 32 headers) Non-auth static headers (Authorization, x-api-key, and !command refused) models[].contextWindow / maxTokens No Integers (1024..10000000 / 1..1048576) Custom model context window and output token caps (defaults 128000 / 16384) models[].reasoning No Boolean (defaults true when thinking != 'off') Declares whether custom model accepts reasoning parameters models[].cost No Object (input, output, optional cacheRead, cacheWrite) USD per million tokens; each rate is 0..1000; input and output are required models[].thinkingLevelMap No Map of level to wire effort or null Custom Pi thinkingLevelMap (null marks a level unsupported) models[].samplingParams No { temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, presence_penalty, repetition_penalty } Default Pi sampling parameters forwarded on outbound model requests models[].samplingParamsByThinkingLevel No Map of thinking level to samplingParams Per-thinking-level sampling parameter overrides models[].compat No Object (thinkingFormat, maxTokensField, zaiToolStream, booleans) OpenAI-compatible dialect flags matching Pi models.json compat Provider-reported cost retains reported provenance. When billing is absent and pricing has a positive rate, Loopwright estimates cost from token usage. Estimated cost is not provider-attested billing; unpriced usage remains unknown.
MCP and limits spec.mcp.servers connects stdio and Streamable http MCP servers on the host and exposes tools as mcp__<id>__<tool>. OAuth MCP declarations fail closed (MCP_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED). spec.limits raises or lowers execution ceilings; Action inputs and LOOPWRIGHT_* variables override manifest values.

selects local process or Streamable HTTP servers[].command / args Conditional Executable / string list (0..32) stdio binary resolved on trusted host PATH and fixed CLI arguments servers[].env / envFrom No String maps (<= 32 entries) Non-secret stdio env values and host secret env bindings (scrubbed automatically) servers[].url Conditional https:// URL Required for http servers (loopback http:// requires custom base URL opt-in) servers[].headersFrom / bearerTokenEnv No Header map / env name Host secret env bindings for HTTP headers or Authorization: Bearer servers[].includeTools / timeoutSeconds No Tool list (1..64) / 5..600 Optional upstream tool allowlist and per-call timeout in seconds (default 60) limits.wallTimeSeconds No Integer (60..21600, default 3600) Total run wall-time budget in seconds (wallTimeMs also accepted) limits.totalTokens No Integer (1000..1000000000, default 20000000) Aggregate input + output token ceiling across all model calls limits.contextWindow No Integer (1024..10000000) Model context window override (LOOPWRIGHT_CONTEXT_WINDOW or context-window overrides) limits.maxOutputTokens No Integer (256..262144, default 32768) Per-call output token ceiling (perCallOutputTokens alias supported) limits.maxModelCalls / maxAttempts No 1..1024 (256) / 1..16 (4) Model turn ceiling and controller attempt ceiling limits.toolTimeoutSeconds No Integer (5..1800, default 300) Per-tool wall-time ceiling in seconds; URL Polls a deterministic JSON release metadata endpoint custom-table Repository table ID Reads a pinned structured version matrix in the repository Verification checks Check and gate fields Field path Required Type and bounds Meaning verification.localChecks Yes Object list (0..32 items) In-host verifiers (candidate mode requires >= 1 local or required gate check) localChecks[].id Yes Identifier (1..64 chars) Unique check ID (cannot use reserved scope, no-change, taskpack-author, taskpack-no-change) localChecks[].implementation Yes Enum (see table below) Built-in verifier bound by compiler to its installed SHA-256 digest localChecks[].parameters Conditional Object Scalar expectations for built-in checks; command.v1 requires its own parameters below verification.externalGates Yes Object list (0..32 items) Remote authenticated gate.v1 checks (pass [] when unused) externalGates[].id Conditional Identifier (1..64 chars) Required per gate item; unique check ID recorded in acceptance evidence externalGates[].gateId Conditional Identifier (1..64 chars) Required per gate item; remote gate policy identifier externalGates[].endpointId Conditional Identifier (1..64 chars) Required per gate item; matches a host HostGateEndpointPlan.id externalGates[].required Conditional Boolean Required per gate item; marks gate receipt mandatory for candidate acceptance Local implementations Implementation Compiler parameters Verification check json-artifact.v1 Binds proposal.path, requiredFields, and schema_version Parses structured candidate artifact and checks required keys and scalars scope.v1 Binds checkId (compiler also runs implicit scope guard) Verifies modified and deleted paths stay inside writable and outside protected no-change.v1 Binds checkId (used automatically in no-change mode) Confirms candidate tree equals base tree when settling as no_change command.v1 Pins script SHA-256 and compiles an authenticated local gate.v1 Runs a protected script against a retained candidate copy Command parameters Parameter Required Type and bounds Meaning script Yes Relative file path, <= 262144 bytes Protected regular script with no symlink ancestors; SHA-256 is checked again before execution timeoutSeconds No Integer (1..3600, default 30) Maximum script execution time allowReadOnlyGitHubToken No Boolean (default false) Passes the resolved GitHub token when available; Output formats spec.output accepts a format string, a list, or an object with a formats list. Omission defaults to json. Action output overrides the taskpack default. The managed CLI selects formats separately with --output-format.

title: Taskpack

content:
Architecture Loopwright runs bounded repository work inside isolated sandboxes and verifies every candidate against independent evidence. Choose between simple repository taskpack automation or fine-grained controller and registry governance.
Contents Execution chain Operating modes Configuration surfaces Runtime baseline Trust boundaries Execution chain Admit: Validate task boundaries and acquire a monotonic SQLite lease fence. Execute: Run an isolated Pi role with trusted host bindings and optional decision routing. Verify: Evaluate the candidate against independent checks and authenticated gate receipts. Publish & Remember: Settle pull request publication and propose reviewed memory separately. Operating modes Loopwright supports two distinct configuration and execution modes sharing one verification kernel:
Dimension Declarative taskpack Managed controller Target user Repository maintainers Platform and security operators Files authored One .loopwright/taskpack.yaml in repo Out-of-repo registry.yaml and controller.yaml Digest pinning Compiled automatically by host Pinned manually via SHA-256 (--registry-sha256) Execution graph Single compiled author + check pipeline Custom multi-step agent and check DAG Credential wiring Mapped from Action or App environment Explicit credentialBindings and path templates Key advantage Zero boilerplate; turnkey triggers and PRs Duty separation, custom gates/MCP, local CLI control Walkthrough Declarative Taskpack Managed Controller Configuration surfaces Every Loopwright document uses apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 across declarative and managed configuration surfaces:
Mode or scope Document kind Top-level keys Reference guide Declarative mode Taskpack apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, spec Taskpack Managed mode TrustedRegistry apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, spec Controller and Registry Managed mode ControllerConfig apiVersion, kind, spec Controller and Registry Managed mode TaskContract apiVersion, kind, spec Task Contract Shared policy spec.sandbox Nested under Taskpack.spec Sandbox Backends Shared policy DecisionPolicy apiVersion, kind, spec Decision Routing Entry points Action or GitHubAppConfig Workflow or apiVersion, kind, spec GitHub Action · GitHub App Runtime baseline Deployment host qualification (qualifyDeploymentHostProfile) enforces these baseline prerequisites across Action, App, and CLI surfaces:
Component Baseline requirement Enforcement scope Node runtime Node.js 26.x (built-in node:sqlite) Required across Action, App, CLI, and workspace builds (gpustack/loopwright provisions it automatically) Package manager npm 11.x Workspace dependency installation and builds Host platform darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, linux/x64 Unlisted OS or architecture targets fail closed Storage and clock Local POSIX filesystem; <= 1000 ms clock drift Network mounts (nfs, smb, fuse, sshfs) and clock jumps fail closed Sandbox backend Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock, or Docker Negotiated against taskpack spec.sandbox policy Optional tools Python 3.11+ (runner bridge); Hugo extended 0.152.2+ (docs site) Needed only when exercising runner helpers or building site/ Trust boundaries Trusted hosts bind credentials, runtimes, handlers, and external services. Taskpacks and model output cannot grant authority. Local fixture proof never establishes live provider or production qualification, and unknown external effects remain unknown until reconciled.
See also — Declarative Taskpack (simple single-file automation) · Managed Controller (fine-grained registry and contract control)

content:
Installation Run Loopwright as a zero-install GitHub Action in target repositories or install the @gpustack/loopwright CLI on a macOS or Linux laptop. After setup, paste a single bootstrap prompt into your coding agent to initialize or migrate repository configuration interactively.
Contents Entry points Prerequisites Step 1: Install CLI Step 2: Verify CLI GitHub Actions Prompt bootstrap Entry points Surface Operating mode Installation method GitHub Action Declarative Taskpack (Simple) Zero local setup; reference uses: gpustack/loopwright@main Laptop CLI (npm / pnpm) Managed Controller or local audit npm install -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright or pnpm add -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright Release tarball Pinned or air-gapped hosts Install gpustack-loopwright-<version>.tgz from GitHub Releases Source checkout Contributors and testers Clone repository, run npm ci && npm run build, and run npm link Prerequisites Local CLI and app-serve hosts must satisfy the runtime baseline : Node.js 26.x (with built-in node:sqlite), npm 11.x, and a local POSIX filesystem on darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, or linux/x64. Provision an approved sandbox backend before executing isolated agent steps.
Step 1: Install CLI npm package Install the single-package CLI globally from npmjs.com using npm or pnpm (--ignore-scripts skips optional transitive lifecycle scripts required by pnpm v10+ build hygiene):
shCopy npm install -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright # or with pnpm: pnpm add -g --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright To run one-off commands without a global install, invoke npx or pnpm dlx:
shCopy npx --ignore-scripts @gpustack/loopwright --help # or with pnpm: pnpm --ignore-scripts dlx @gpustack/loopwright --help Release archive Install an immutable release archive directly from GitHub Releases (replace 0.1.0 with the published version):
shCopy npm install -g --ignore-scripts https://github.com/gpustack/loopwright/releases/download/v0.1.0/gpustack-loopwright-0.1.0.tgz Source build Clone the repository to develop locally or test unreleased commits:
shCopy git clone https://github.com/gpustack/loopwright.git cd loopwright npm ci npm run build npm link Step 2: Verify CLI Confirm the binary resolves on your PATH:
shCopy loopwright --version loopwright --help For Managed Controller runs, loopwright init --directory "$HOME/loopwright-ops" writes low-level controller.draft.yaml and registry.draft.yaml skeletons (0600). To initialize a repository .loopwright/taskpack.yaml or migrate existing sync scripts without manual boilerplate, use the interactive bootstrap prompt below.
GitHub Actions Consumer repositories using Declarative Taskpack mode do not need local CLI installation. Add .loopwright/taskpack.yaml and reference gpustack/loopwright@main in .github/workflows/loopwright.yml:
yamlCopy name: loopwright on: workflow_dispatch: {} permissions: contents: read jobs: taskpack: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: gpustack/loopwright@main with: taskpack-path: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml event-name: ${{ github.event_name }} event-path: ${{ github.event_path }} dry-run: 'true' The composite Action provisions Node.js 26 automatically on the runner. Follow GitHub Action for App token wiring and secret bindings.
Prompt bootstrap No custom skill or plugin is required to author Loopwright YAML. Open your coding agent inside the target repository (for example, when migrating an existing automatic synchronized workflow) and paste one prompt:
Taskpack prompt textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and fetch the Markdown guides for Declarative Taskpack, Taskpack, and GitHub Action. Inspect this repository (including any existing automatic synchronized workflows, scripts, version tables, and directory layout), confirm my upstream sources, writable/protected paths, verification checks, and PR settings with me, then generate .loopwright/taskpack.yaml and .github/workflows/loopwright.yml (apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1) without hardcoding secrets. Controller prompt textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and fetch the Markdown guides for Managed Controller, Task Contract, and Controller and Registry. Help me design an out-of-repo TrustedRegistry (registry.yaml) and SHA-256-pinned ControllerConfig (controller.yaml) for this repository, compute the local Loopwright handler and graph digests, and verify the plan with loopwright check. See also — Declarative Taskpack (simple automated repository mode) · Managed Controller (fine-grained registry and contract mode)
Next → Declarative Taskpack — author or migrate a .loopwright/taskpack.yaml workflow.
title: Installation

content:
CLI The CLI validates trusted configuration and manages bounded local runs. Install the loopwright command on your laptop first via Installation , then use it to prepare, inspect, resume, or reconcile work and audit capability closure.
Contents Step 1: Generate drafts Step 2: Approve bindings Step 3: Check configuration Step 4: Run work Step 5: Inspect recovery Step 6: Audit closure Command reference Exit codes Step 1: Generate drafts shCopy loopwright init --directory ./loopwright-config The command creates controller.draft.yaml, registry.draft.yaml, and README.draft.md for Managed Controller workflows (for a complete populated setup, follow Managed Controller ). Note that loopwright init does not generate .loopwright/taskpack.yaml; to bootstrap or migrate a repository Taskpack interactively, use the llms.txt bootstrap prompt .
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TrustedRegistry metadata: name: operator-draft spec: version: 1 resourceVersion: context-draft handlers: [] roleProfiles: [] runtimeProfiles: [] resources: [] credentialBindings: [] environmentBindings: [] Draft: The excerpt shows the generated registry; controller.draft.yaml contains REVIEW_REQUIRED placeholders that must be replaced before execution. Authority: Keep approved registry bytes and run state outside the checkout. Context: proven_bound is the strict default; estimated guards require explicit immutable opt-in. File Purpose controller.draft.yaml Task, registry name + digest, profile references, and controls registry.draft.yaml Trusted handlers, profiles, resources, and bindings README.draft.md Draft readiness and review instructions Step 2: Approve bindings Review the task scope, exact installed profiles, handlers, credentials, and registry bytes. Replace every placeholder and calculate the SHA-256 of the final approved registry. The generated digest matches only the initial draft bytes.
Step 3: Check configuration shCopy loopwright check --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --json loopwright run --dry-run --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --json Both commands validate and compile statically. Neither proves execution readiness, provider availability, or host qualification.
Step 4: Run work shCopy loopwright run --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo loopwright resume --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo Use resume for an existing run with the same trusted identity and bindings. Do not replay an uncertain external effect.
run, resume, and reconcile accept --output-format <csv> with json, github-step-summary, markdown, and text. Use --step-summary-file <path> to select the summary file. With --json, stdout stays pure NDJSON. The CLI does not emit selected Markdown or text reports in this mode. Use --step-summary-file to write a separate Markdown summary. Without --json, selected reports go to stdout.
Step 5: Inspect recovery shCopy loopwright status --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --json loopwright inspect --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --output INSPECTION_DIR --json loopwright reconcile --config CONFIG --registry REGISTRY --registry-sha256 DIGEST --repo REPO --run-root TRUSTED_ROOT --run-id demo --receipt RECEIPT --json Inspect state and evidence before recovery. Reconcile an unknown external outcome with its matching authenticated receipt; absent evidence stays unknown.
Step 6: Audit closure shCopy loopwright closure --verify-failures --json Closure exits 0 for a valid report, 3 for falsification or unsupported capability, 4 for failure-matrix failure, and 8 for integrity failure. JSON output uses versioned envelopes with kind, sequence, run identity, and data.
Disposition Evidence scope Meaning closed_local Recorded local evidence level Local criterion and failure matrix passed blocked_external Unprovisioned external dependency Live service, host, or hardware remains external deferred_owned Deferred owned capability Recorded prerequisite remains unimplemented or deferred Command reference Subcommand Required flags Optional flags Purpose init --directory --force, --json Emit controller.draft.yaml and registry.draft.yaml check --config, --registry, --registry-sha256 --output, --json Compile and verify configuration and registry digest statically run --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, --repo, --run-root, --run-id --json, --output-format, --step-summary-file Execute a bounded controller run run --dry-run --dry-run, --config, --registry, --registry-sha256 --output, --json Compile plan statically (--repo, --run-root, --run-id disallowed) resume --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, --repo, --run-root, --run-id --json, --output-format, --step-summary-file Resume an existing run under identical trusted bindings status --run-root, --run-id --json Read current run stage, lease state, and checkpoint summary inspect --run-root, --run-id --output, --json Export redacted run receipts, checkpoints, and diagnostics reconcile --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, --repo, --run-root, --run-id, --receipt --output, --json, --output-format, --step-summary-file Settle an unknown external outcome with an authenticated receipt closure None --repo, --output, --verify-failures, --json Audit the 23-capability closure matrix and 14-case failure suite app-serve --config --repo, --json Start the opt-in GitHub App HTTP webhook and token listener shCopy loopwright app-serve --config github-app.yaml --repo . --json Set spec.listen.enabled: true first. The command exits 2 for disabled or invalid configuration, 130 on SIGINT, and 143 on SIGTERM. See GitHub App for configuration and host requirements.
Exit codes Code Meaning 0 Completed, no change, or successful static command 2 Usage or configuration rejected 3 Unsupported capability or blocked work 4 Execution or acceptance failed 5 Allowance exhausted 6 Deadline expired 7 Reconciliation or ownership needed 8 Authoritative result unavailable or incident 130 Accounted SIGINT, subject to uncertainty precedence 143 Accounted SIGTERM, subject to uncertainty precedence See also — Installation (install @gpustack/loopwright and copy bootstrap prompts) · Controller and Registry (approve trusted execution bindings)
Next → Managed Controller — populate registry.yaml and controller.yaml end to end.
title: CLI

content:
GitHub Action The reusable Action runs a taskpack cycle in a consumer repository without a resident server. It discovers upstream changes, verifies candidates, and can publish a managed pull request.
Contents Workflow Execution and publication Secrets and environment Inputs Outputs Triggers Workflow Install a taskpack and configure the provider and App secrets before enabling this workflow. The App installation needs repository contents and pull request write permissions for native publication.
yamlCopy name: loopwright on: schedule: - cron: '0 3 * * *' workflow_dispatch: {} issue_comment: types: [created] permissions: contents: read jobs: taskpack: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 persist-credentials: false - uses: gpustack/loopwright@main id: loopwright with: taskpack-path: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml # Optional event-name: ${{ github.event_name }} event-path: ${{ github.event_path }} github-app-id: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_ID }} github-app-private-key: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }} github-app-installation-id: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_INSTALLATION_ID }} output: json,github-step-summary # Optional env: ZAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }} Taskpack: Set publication to pull_request to enable native PR publication, or disabled to omit it. Provider: Set the token variable for the selected model, not necessarily ZAI_API_KEY. Runtime: The Action sets up Node.js 26 and builds the workspace if its entrypoint is absent. Dry run: Set dry-run: 'true' to compile without running the controller. Execution and publication A live Action resolves repository identity and revisions, discovers upstreams, and looks for an existing managed PR. It compiles trusted artifacts outside the checkout, then runs the controller for admitted work.
Stage Behavior Discover Read GitHub releases, Git tags or commits, HTTP JSON, or custom tables; compare versions with the proposal. Execute Author a candidate and verify scope and configured checks; eligible failures can enter bounded repair. Publish For pull_request mode, create or update a managed PR after verification. Use upstream-records to supply precomputed acquisition records instead of live discovery. Matching upstream state can settle as no_change. Unavailable upstreams can block execution.
Native publication uses a detached git worktree, a signed-off diff-only commit, and --force-with-lease. It does not embed credentials in remote URLs. An uncertain external outcome remains unknown; do not silently retry it.
Local command.v1 checks run through a signed loopback gate against a verified candidate snapshot. The Action verifies each script digest and passes a limited environment. If a check opts into a GitHub token, it receives the resolved token; grant that token only the permissions the check may use.
On GitHub Actions, an omitted spec.sandbox selects direct-dedicated. This uses host process isolation, not a container security boundary. The turnkey host session supports macos-seatbelt, linux-bwrap, linux-landlock, and direct-dedicated, and blocks docker. See Sandbox Backends for isolation tradeoffs.
Protected paths override writable paths. Workflow files and taskpack control assets remain protected. See Taskpack for scope, instructions, and check configuration.
Secrets and environment Pass a token with github-token, or provide all three App inputs to mint an installation token inside the Action. A nonempty github-token takes precedence, followed by GITHUB_TOKEN; either prevents App token minting. GH_TOKEN is not the Action token fallback.
The App ID and installation ID must be positive integers. The private key is a PEM secret. Restrict installation access to the target repository and required permissions. App tokens can trigger downstream workflows under GitHub’s App event rules.
Credential Purpose github-token or GITHUB_TOKEN GitHub discovery and native PR publication; permissions depend on the operations used. github-app-id, github-app-private-key, github-app-installation-id Mint an installation token when no direct token is supplied. Provider token environment Authenticate live model calls; token variables can contain comma-separated token pools. LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET Sign external gate requests when a gate endpoint is configured. LOOPWRIGHT_PUBLICATION_SIGNING_SECRET Sign requests to an external publication endpoint. Local command gates and native publication use ephemeral loopback credentials. They do not require external endpoint signing secrets. Generated registry and controller files contain secret references, not raw credentials. Never commit secrets to the repository.
Inputs All Action inputs are optional. Conditional credentials, endpoint bindings, and event payloads depend on the taskpack and trigger.
Input Default Purpose taskpack-path .loopwright/taskpack.yaml Repository-relative manifest path, including a custom control directory. mode candidate candidate or no-change cycle mode. event-name workflow_dispatch GitHub event name; pass github.event_name for other triggers. event-path Unset Event payload path; pass github.event_path for comment and review events. run-root RUNNER_TEMP or ../.loopwright-runs Trusted artifact root outside the checkout. run-id GITHUB_RUN_ID or local Stable run identifier. storage-profile actions-basic Host storage profile: actions-basic or durable. provider, model, thinking Taskpack model pool Override author model selection; thinking levels range from off to max. api, base-url Inferred, unset Wire API and trusted HTTPS endpoint override; base-url requires api. provider-token-env Provider default Environment variable containing a provider token or comma-separated pool. models-json Unset Trusted Pi model configuration path; shell credential resolvers are refused. allow-custom-base-url false Set true to permit model base URLs declared in the taskpack. dry-run false Set true to compile without executing the controller. gate-endpoint-url Unset External gate endpoint, bound as default. publication-endpoint-url Unset External managed publication endpoint; otherwise native PR publication is available. output Taskpack formats or json Comma-separated output formats; overrides spec.output.formats. github-token GITHUB_TOKEN or unset GitHub token for discovery, opted-in checks, and publication. github-app-id Unset App ID for installation token minting. github-app-private-key Unset App PEM private key for installation token minting. github-app-installation-id Unset Installation ID for token minting. upstream-records Unset JSON array of precomputed upstream acquisition records. mcp-servers Taskpack spec.mcp.servers JSON or YAML MCP server declarations merged by id (LOOPWRIGHT_MCP_SERVERS fallback). wall-time-seconds 3600 Run wall-time limit override in seconds (60..21600; LOOPWRIGHT_WALL_TIME_SECONDS). total-tokens 20000000 Total token ceiling across model calls (1000..1000000000; LOOPWRIGHT_TOTAL_TOKENS). context-window Model catalog or 128000 Model context window token override (1024..10000000; LOOPWRIGHT_CONTEXT_WINDOW). max-output-tokens 32768 Per-call output token ceiling (256..262144; LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS). max-model-calls 256 Maximum model call count per run (1..1024; LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS). max-attempts 4 Maximum controller attempt count (1..16; LOOPWRIGHT_MAX_ATTEMPTS). tool-timeout-seconds 300 Per-tool execution timeout in seconds (5..1800; LOOPWRIGHT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). command-timeout-seconds 30 (<= 3600) command.v1 local check timeout override (1..3600; LOOPWRIGHT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). Limit overrides apply in strict order (INPUT_* > LOOPWRIGHT_* > spec.limits > compiler defaults). Additional byte and session ceilings (LOOPWRIGHT_RESPONSE_BYTES, LOOPWRIGHT_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES, LOOPWRIGHT_FILE_BYTES, LOOPWRIGHT_SESSION_BYTES) also accept environment overrides. Interactive OAuth and CLI providers or MCP servers are unsupported. Model and MCP options are listed in Taskpack .
Outputs The Action writes a compact, scrubbed result JSON summary (with SHA-256 digests and byte lengths rather than raw binary buffers) to stdout and GITHUB_OUTPUT. Live runs stream [loopwright] progress lines (upstream discovery, connected MCP servers, per-turn token/duration metrics, tool calls, and check outcomes) plus a plain-text run summary to stderr. A compiled result alone does not establish successful publication; inspect delegateOutcome and the run report.
Output Meaning result Compact structured entrypoint summary and delegateOutcome (ok, detail). pr-url Published PR URL when available; otherwise empty. total-tokens Exact integer token subtotal, or 0 when usage is unavailable. cost-usd Six-decimal USD known subtotal when cost provenance is reported or estimated; otherwise omitted. Extended outputs are written for live runs, or for dry runs with an explicit output input. Step summaries and human-readable reports format token counts using K/M/B and elapsed durations using ms/s/m/h, while total-tokens and JSON reports preserve exact integer counts. Estimated cost uses model pricing and is not provider-attested billing. A missing cost is unknown, not zero.
Format Destination json Structured Action result remains on stdout and GITHUB_OUTPUT. github-step-summary Markdown report appended to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when available. markdown Human-readable report on stderr. text Plain-text report on stderr. totalTokens is the primary usage metric across sinks, with inputTokens and outputTokens breakdowns when available. Human-readable summaries show cost only for reported or estimated provenance. Reports include usage provenance when available. Output is scrubbed and workflow command text is neutralized. Local and fixture tests do not qualify live GitHub publication or provider billing.
Triggers Intake supports schedule, manual dispatch, repository dispatch, release, issue comment, and pull request review events, subject to taskpack policy. Pass the event name and payload explicitly as shown above. Comment commands also require actor authorization.
Install a workflow in each consumer repository. For centralized webhook intake and token brokering, see GitHub App .
See also — GitHub App (configure webhook intake) · Sandbox Backends (select execution isolation)
Next → Declarative Taskpack — configure the repository manifest.
title: GitHub Action

content:
GitHub App GitHub Action mode is the primary zero-server path for consumer repositories. Use gpustack/loopwright@main for scheduled runs, manual dispatch, and /loopwright comment commands.
The resident HTTP daemon is disabled by default. Operators can opt in for centralized webhook queuing and token brokering; production requires separately qualified ingress and host infrastructure.
Contents App registration Admission and permissions GitHubAppConfig Control plane Host qualification App registration Create a GitHub App in your personal Developer settings or organization settings (https://github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/apps), then install it on the target repositories.
Setting Value Contents Read and write Pull requests Read and write Issues Read and write Metadata Read-only Webhooks Inactive for Action mode; active for app-serve Events For app-serve: Issue comment, Pull request review, Release App secrets Repository or organization secrets: LOOPWRIGHT_APP_ID, LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY Webhook secret LOOPWRIGHT_WEBHOOK_SECRET when app-serve is enabled Use actions/create-github-app-token@v1 with gpustack/loopwright@main in the consumer workflow . The App’s webhook secret and private key must also be available in the trusted daemon environment when enabled.
Admission and permissions Subscribe only to the event types used by your taskpack, including release, issue comment and pull request review as needed. Comment commands are restricted to authorized actors. Verify X-Hub-Signature-256 over raw request bytes with HMAC-SHA256; mismatches and conflicting delivery IDs fail closed. The receiver implements verification before intake.
Installation tokens are restricted to one repository. The read_only profile grants contents and metadata read; publish_pull_request grants contents and pull requests write plus metadata read. Store the App private key and webhook secret in trusted host secret storage.
GitHubAppConfig Save the daemon configuration as github-app.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: GitHubAppConfig spec: appId: '12345' webhookSecretEnv: LOOPWRIGHT_WEBHOOK_SECRET privateKeyEnv: LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY apiBaseUrl: https://api.github.com # Optional (defaults to https://api.github.com) listen: # Optional block (set enabled to true for loopwright app-serve) enabled: false # Optional (defaults to false) host: 127.0.0.1 port: 8787 webhookPath: /webhooks/github # Optional (defaults to /webhooks/github) tokenTtlSeconds: 600 # Optional (defaults to 600) maxPayloadBytes: 1048576 # Optional (defaults to 1048576) taskpackPath: .loopwright/taskpack.yaml # Optional repo-relative taskpack path operatorAllowlist: # Optional GitHub login allowlist for slash commands - release-operator Secrets: Provide environment variable names, not secret values. Listen: Add authenticated ingress before serving external webhooks. Path: The taskpack path must be relative and cannot traverse directories. Field path Required Default Bounds and constraint apiVersion Yes — Must be 'loopwright.dev/v1alpha1' kind Yes — Must be 'GitHubAppConfig' (<= 64 KiB file) spec.appId Yes — Non-empty GitHub App numeric ID or slug (1–64 chars) spec.webhookSecretEnv Yes — Uppercase env var name ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) holding HMAC secret spec.privateKeyEnv Yes — Uppercase env var name ([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) holding App PEM spec.apiBaseUrl No https://api.github.com HTTPS URL, or loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1 / localhost / [::1]) spec.listen Conditional Unset Optional mapping; required with enabled: true to run app-serve spec.listen.enabled No false Set true to enable loopwright app-serve spec.listen.host Conditional 127.0.0.1 Required when spec.listen is present; keep tenant routes private spec.listen.port Conditional 8787 Required when spec.listen is present; integer 0–65535 spec.listen.webhookPath No /webhooks/github Leading / path; cannot collide with /healthz or /tenants/* spec.tokenTtlSeconds No 600 Integer 60–3600 cached installation token ceiling spec.maxPayloadBytes No 1048576 Integer 1024–26214400 inbound webhook byte cap spec.taskpackPath No Unset Relative regular-file path validated at startup spec.operatorAllowlist No Unset GitHub login list (1–64 entries) authorized for slash commands Control plane Set spec.listen.enabled: true, bind the named secrets in the trusted environment, then start the daemon:
shCopy loopwright app-serve --config github-app.yaml --repo . The command applies the configured listener and token broker settings. It refuses disabled or invalid configuration. The loader resolves the named webhook secret and private key from the environment.
The service binds loopback by default. Provide authenticated ingress and a configured broker in the trusted host; do not expose tenant lease endpoints publicly. Endpoints include the configured listen.webhookPath (default /webhooks/github), /healthz, and tenant lease and settle routes. The broker issues scoped short-lived tokens and scrubs secrets from responses.
Webhook events Event Trigger surface Admission rule release Published upstream release Enabled via spec.triggers.releasePublished issue_comment Issue or PR /loopwright command Requires collaborator or operatorAllowlist actor pull_request_review Managed PR review comment Requires authorized actor and enabled command schedule Cron workflow run Enabled via spec.triggers.schedule workflow_dispatch Manual operator trigger Enabled via spec.triggers.workflowDispatch repository_dispatch Automation dispatch payload Subject to intake signature and trigger policy Intake dispositions Disposition Queue action Meaning ready Enqueued for tenant Signature, actor, and trigger checks passed no_change Settled without run Upstream discovery found no eligible change blocked Rejected before run Policy, authorization, or payload check refused intake Host qualification Verify the host against the runtime baseline and required sandbox backends before starting app-serve. Interactive MCP OAuth challenges and unsandboxed fallbacks fail closed (MCP_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED, SANDBOX_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT).
In-memory queue and delivery state do not establish durable cross-restart recovery.
