title: GitHub App

content:
Declarative Taskpack Declarative taskpack mode is Loopwright’s simple automated workflow for repository maintainers. Author one .loopwright/taskpack.yaml file in your repository, and the GitHub Action or App compiles contracts, handler digests, and registry bindings automatically.
For strict separation between task authors and platform-owned TrustedRegistry files, custom multi-step DAGs, or local CLI execution, follow Managed Controller instead.
Contents Overview Prompt bootstrap Step 1: Author taskpack Step 2: Validate taskpack Step 3: Configure workflow Step 4: Review outcomes Overview Declarative taskpack mode eliminates manual boilerplate while preserving every Loopwright safety boundary:
Responsibility Authored in taskpack Compiled by Loopwright Work scope Optionally declare writable and protected paths Adds control paths and built-in masks; protected paths take precedence Execution Declare upstreams and proposal artifact Compiles TaskContract, ControllerConfig, and TrustedRegistry (0600) Digests None required Computes SHA-256 digests for installed handlers and package-lock.json Secrets Pass GitHub Secrets to Action or App env Generates scoped ${ENV} credential bindings and scrubs logs Settlement Choose pull_request or disabled Opens head-pinned PRs or settles verified no_change runs Prompt bootstrap loopwright init only scaffolds low-level controller drafts; it does not inspect your repository. To initialize .loopwright/taskpack.yaml from scratch or migrate an existing automatic synchronized workflow, paste this prompt into your coding agent inside the target repository:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and follow the Markdown links for Declarative Taskpack, Taskpack, and GitHub Action. Inspect this repository (especially existing automatic synchronized workflows, scripts, version manifests, and docs/config directories), ask me to confirm any ambiguous upstream sources, writable/protected scope, or checks, and generate .loopwright/taskpack.yaml plus .github/workflows/loopwright.yml using apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1. Through normal back-and-forth conversation, the agent reads the live Loopwright specification from llms.txt, maps your existing sync logic into upstreams, scope, proposal, and verification, and tells you which GitHub Secrets to configure.
Step 1: Author taskpack Create .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml in the target repository. Loopwright derives .auto-sync as the control root.
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: Taskpack metadata: name: docs-sync spec: goal: candidate: Refresh documentation from upstream releases and pass local checks. noChange: Confirm upstream documentation needs no update and settle as no change. scope: # Optional protected: - docs/protected-notes.md instructions: # Optional - .auto-sync/prompts/instructions.md upstreams: - id: engine kind: github-release source: octocat/engine watchedPaths: - docs allowPrerelease: false # Optional (defaults to false) proposal: path: docs/proposal.json requiredFields: - schema_version - candidates schemaVersion: 1 verification: localChecks: - id: docs-proposal-json implementation: json-artifact.v1 - id: verify-docs implementation: command.v1 parameters: script: .auto-sync/checks/verify.sh timeoutSeconds: 30 # Optional externalGates: [] # Optional remote gate checks publication: mode: pull_request targetBranch: main headBranchPrefix: loopwright-docs- titleTemplate: "docs - sync upstream documentation" memory: directory: .auto-sync/memory/docs-sync apply: separate-pull-request onNoModelBudget: deterministic-observations-only triggers: schedule: true workflowDispatch: true releasePublished: false commentCommands: - retry - revise - status commentPrefixes: # Optional (defaults to ['/loopwright']) - /loopwright models: # Optional ordered model pool - provider: zai id: glm-5.3 thinking: high # Optional apiKeyEnv: ZAI_API_KEY # Optional - provider: zai-coding-cn # Optional fallback candidate id: glm-5.3 thinking: high # Optional apiKeyEnv: ZAI_CODING_CN_API_KEY # Optional output: # Optional formats: - json - github-step-summary decisions: # Optional System-One triage policy enabled: true provider: typesafe-jev # Optional disclosurePolicy: public-metadata-only # Optional minConfidence: 0.8 # Optional confirmThreshold: 0.6 # Optional hardDeadlineMs: 5000 # Optional maxAttempts: 1 # Optional allowImages: false # Optional Field dictionary: Inspect every field, bound, and enum in Taskpack . Scope: Omitted writable permits **, except effective protected paths. Protected paths always win. Inputs: Create the instruction file and verification script before running. Loopwright pins and protects both files. Proposal: The proposal must be writable and end in .yaml, .yml, or .json. Secrets: Never place tokens or ${ENV} templates inside taskpack.yaml; the parser rejects untrusted interpolation. Step 2: Validate taskpack Verify your host meets the runtime baseline , then test compilation in dry-run mode before enabling live mutations.
Run the GitHub Action with dry-run: 'true' in a pull request workflow, or call loadDeclarativeTaskpack and compileDeclarativeTaskpack in a local check script. Dry-run mode validates the manifest, negotiates sandbox capabilities, and compiles config.yaml and registry.yaml without invoking model providers or pushing branches.
Step 3: Configure workflow Add .github/workflows/loopwright.yml to your repository to run on schedule, workflow_dispatch, or /loopwright issue comments:
yamlCopy name: Loopwright Sync on: schedule: - cron: '0 4 * * *' workflow_dispatch: issue_comment: types: [created] permissions: contents: read jobs: sync: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1 # Optional when minting App PR tokens id: app-token with: app-id: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_ID }} private-key: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }} - uses: gpustack/loopwright@main with: taskpack-path: .auto-sync/taskpack.yaml # Optional custom control root github-token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }} event-name: ${{ github.event_name }} # Optional (defaults to GITHUB_EVENT_NAME) event-path: ${{ github.event_path }} # Optional for schedule/manual; needed on comments dry-run: 'false' # Optional (defaults to 'false') env: ZAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }} # Optional in dry-run mode LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET: ${{ secrets.LOOPWRIGHT_GATE_SIGNING_SECRET }} # Optional when externalGates is empty Action inputs and secrets: Review every input, output, and secret variable in GitHub Action . Centralized webhook server: Deploy a multi-repository intake server via GitHub App . Step 4: Review outcomes Reports include total tokens, with input and output breakdowns. Cost appears in human-readable summaries only when reported or estimated.
Candidate pull request: When upstream changes require edits and every check passes, Loopwright opens or updates a head-pinned pull request matching headBranchPrefix. Verified no-change: When no update is needed, the compiled no-change.v1 check verifies an untouched tree and settles cleanly without opening an empty PR. Slash-command iteration: Collaborators with write access comment /loopwright status, /loopwright retry, or /loopwright revise on managed issues or pull requests. Reviewed memory: Memory proposals target .loopwright/memory/<name> via a separate pull request so candidate diffs never self-approve retained memory. See also — Taskpack (every Taskpack field and enum) · Managed Controller (fine-grained out-of-repo contract and registry workflow)

Managed Controller Managed controller mode is Loopwright’s fine-grained governance workflow for platform engineers and local CLI operators. You author an out-of-repo TrustedRegistry, pin its SHA-256 digest inside ControllerConfig alongside a TaskContract DAG, and drive admission, execution, inspection, and crash reconciliation via the loopwright CLI.
For single-file repository automation where Loopwright compiles contracts and digests automatically, follow Declarative Taskpack instead.
Contents Configuration relationships Overview Prompt bootstrap Step 1: Generate drafts Step 2: Pin registry Step 3: Author controller Step 4: Execute run Step 5: Reconcile receipts Configuration relationships Managed controller mode coordinates an operator-owned authority store (TrustedRegistry) with a run configuration (ControllerConfig embedding TaskContract):
Relationship Source field Target declaration Runtime invariant Containment ControllerConfig.spec.task Embedded TaskContract (apiVersion, kind, spec) JCS-hashed into run lock; carries zero credentials or handler digests Registry hash lock ControllerConfig.spec.registry.{name,digest} TrustedRegistry.metadata.name + file SHA-256 Must match --registry-sha256 and live outside repo/config roots Role binding spec.profiles.roles[].{roleId,profileRef} Bridges TaskContract.roles[].id to roleProfiles[].id Enforces provider, context ceiling, tool subset, and runtimeRef Step & check binding spec.profiles.steps[].{stepId,handlerRef} Bridges TaskContract.steps[].id to handlers[].id Verifies installed handler SHA-256 and acceptance.checks[].id Context pinning TaskContract.trustedContext.{revision,resources} TrustedRegistry.{resourceVersion,resources[]} Matches context revision and read-only instruction SHA-256 digests Secret & PR wiring spec.credentials[] & publication.endpointRef credentialBindings[], environmentBindings[], publicationEndpoints[] Resolves ${ENV} in memory only; signs HMAC PR/gate requests Overview Prompt bootstrap loopwright init writes generic REVIEW_REQUIRED placeholders. To assemble tailored registry.yaml and controller.yaml files interactively without looking up digests by hand, paste this prompt into your local coding agent:
textCopy Read https://docs.gpustack.ai/loopwright/llms.txt and fetch the Markdown guides for Managed Controller, Task Contract, and Controller and Registry. Inspect this target repository, confirm my writable/protected scope, budgets, and required checks, compute the installed Loopwright handler and graph SHA-256 digests on this machine, write out-of-repo registry.yaml and controller.yaml, and validate them with loopwright check. Step 1: Generate drafts Install @gpustack/loopwright (see Installation ) and initialize starter YAML files in a real non-symlink directory outside the target repository:
shCopy mkdir -p "$HOME/loopwright-ops" "$HOME/loopwright-runs" "$HOME/loopwright-trust" loopwright init --directory "$HOME/loopwright-ops" cp "$HOME/loopwright-ops/registry.draft.yaml" "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" cp "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.draft.yaml" "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" loopwright init writes 0600 drafts. Keep registry.yaml in $HOME/loopwright-trust outside cwd, outside $HOME/loopwright-ops, and outside any target repository (REGISTRY_UNTRUSTED).
Step 2: Pin registry Compute the installed handler and runtime digests from your Loopwright installation so registry.yaml pins verified code bytes:
shCopy node --input-type=module -e " import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; import { installedHandlerDigests } from '@loopwright/controller'; import { describePiAdapterFiles } from '@loopwright/agent-pi'; const handlers = await installedHandlerDigests(); const pi = await describePiAdapterFiles(); const lock = readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../package-lock.json', import.meta.resolve('@loopwright/agent-pi')))); console.log({ handlers, pi, graphSha256: createHash('sha256').update(lock).digest('hex') }); " Populate $HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml (metadata.name is referenced by controller.yaml):

id: zai-token consumer: provider destinationRef: zai environmentNames: - ZAI_API_KEY template: ${ZAI_API_KEY} environmentBindings: - name: ZAI_API_KEY classification: credential paths: - /spec/credentials/0/template Compute and export the SHA-256 digest of the finalized registry.yaml:
shCopy REGISTRY_SHA=$(shasum -a 256 "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" | awk '{print $1}') echo "$REGISTRY_SHA" Step 3: Author controller Edit $HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml to embed your TaskContract, bind registry.name + $REGISTRY_SHA, and map roles and steps:
yamlCopy apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: ControllerConfig spec: registry: name: prod-operator-registry digest: algorithm: sha256 hex: <hash> task: apiVersion: loopwright.dev/v1alpha1 kind: TaskContract spec: goal: Update packages/app/manifest.json release metadata and pass JSON validation. taskpack: app-manifest target: repository: acme/example-app baseRevision: main sourceRevision: v1.4.0 matrix: null scope: writable: - "packages/app/**" protected: - "packages/app/policy/**" roles: - id: builder adapter: pi provider: zai model: glm-5.3 thinking: high tools: - read - write - edit trustedContext: revision: rev-2026-11 discovery: disabled resources: [] budgets: wallTimeMs: 300000 # Must exceed controls.drainReserveMs (120000 ms). totalTokens: 64000 perCallOutputTokens: 1024 maxModelCalls: 8 maxConcurrency: 1 maxFormatRepairs: 1 maxImplementationRepairs: 2 maxTransportRetries: 1 enforcement: wallTime: hard_admission tokens: soft_accounting modelCalls: hard_admission concurrency: hard_admission formatRepairs: hard_admission implementationRepairs: hard_admission transportRetries: hard_admission steps: - id: author-change kind: agent uses: pi-author roleId: builder dependsOn: [] - id: verify-manifest kind: check uses: check-manifest-json roleId: null dependsOn: - author-change acceptance: required: - manifest-json checks: - id: manifest-json allowedEvidenceLevels: - local_execution profiles: roles: - roleId: builder profileRef: builder-profile steps: - stepId: author-change handlerRef: pi-author - stepId: verify-manifest handlerRef: check-manifest-json credentials: - ref: zai-token template: ${ZAI_API_KEY} controls: drainReserveMs: 120000 maxAttempts: 4 repeatFailureLimit: 2 submission: mode: artifact_or_assistant path: null publication: mode: disabled Contract fields: See Task Contract for every TaskContract field and budget invariant. Registry and controller fields: See Controller and Registry for every TrustedRegistry and ControllerConfig field. Step 4: Execute run Run static compilation first (check performs zero network calls and zero state admission), then launch the fenced run outside $HOME/loopwright-trust:
shCopy export ZAI_API_KEY="zai_example_token" loopwright check --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --json loopwright run --config "$HOME/loopwright-ops/controller.yaml" --registry "$HOME/loopwright-trust/registry.yaml" --registry-sha256 "$REGISTRY_SHA" --repo /path/to/example-app --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --json Step 5: Reconcile receipts Query run state, export evidence bundles, or resume/reconcile interrupted executions:
shCopy loopwright status --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --json loopwright inspect --run-root "$HOME/loopwright-runs" --run-id run-20261112-01 --output "$HOME/loopwright-runs/bundle-01" Resume after host restart: Run loopwright resume with the same --run-root, --run-id, --config, --registry, --registry-sha256, and --repo. Reconcile uncertain publication (exit 7): Never retry uncertain remote mutations blindly; verify remote state and settle with loopwright reconcile ... --receipt receipt.json (see CLI ). content:
Documentation Loopwright supports two operating modes sharing one verification kernel: Declarative Taskpack (single-file automated repository sync via GitHub Action or App) and Managed Controller (fine-grained out-of-repo TrustedRegistry and TaskContract governance via the CLI).
Getting Started Architecture explains the four-stage execution chain, the two operating modes, and the runtime baseline. Installation installs @gpustack/loopwright, wires GitHub Actions, and provides llms.txt bootstrap prompts. Operations GitHub Action configures the reusable Action and secret bindings in workflows. GitHub App deploys the webhook and token-brokering control plane. CLI runs local compilation, execution, inspection, reconciliation, and closure audits. Walkthroughs Declarative Taskpack walks through simple single-file repository automation and automatic synchronized workflow migration. Managed Controller walks through fine-grained out-of-repo TrustedRegistry, ControllerConfig, and CLI execution. Configuration Taskpack documents every field and enum in .loopwright/taskpack.yaml (Taskpack). Task Contract documents every field, budget, step, and evidence tier in TaskContract. Controller and Registry documents every handler, profile, credential, endpoint, and control in TrustedRegistry and ControllerConfig. Sandbox Backends covers native OS and container sandbox policies and capabilities. Decision Routing details System-One advisory confidence zones, providers, and disclosure policies.
